ai.description: This slender snake reaches 40 cm. It is sandy-brown with dark dorsal blotches and a white belly. Key features include a sharply pointed, shovel-like snout and a distinctly upturned rostral scale.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Sindh Awl-headed Snake is best distinguished by its sharply upturned, shovel-like snout, which is significantly more pointed and prominent than in other local colubrids.
ai.habitat: The Sindh Awl-headed Snake inhabits arid, sandy deserts and semi-desert scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically at low altitudes within sparsely vegetated plains.
ai.behavior: The Sindh Awl-headed snake is primarily nocturnal and uses its specialized, shovel-shaped snout to burrow through loose desert sands in search of lizard eggs and prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Lytorhynchus paradoxus* is oviparous, laying small clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Sindh Awl-headed Snake occurs in the arid regions of Pakistan’s Sindh and Punjab provinces, typically inhabiting sandy deserts at low elevations.
